chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the Interpreter, may God be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us, on the authority of their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, upon them be peace, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding the words of God, the Exalted and Mighty:
It is He who created for you all that is on the earth; then He directed Himself to the heaven and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.

He said: 'He is the One who created for you all that is on the earth so that you may take heed through it and attain His pleasure through it and guard yourselves against the punishment of His Fire through it. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, took charge of its creation and perfection, and made it seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things. And because of His knowledge of all things, He knew what is beneficial, so He created for you all that is on the earth for your benefit, O Children of Adam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of earthly creation according to Imam Ali's interpretation of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:29?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ali ibn Musa (al-Rida) elucidates the teleological purpose of creation, interpreting the phrase 'created for you all that is on the earth' as a means for humans to attain divine pleasure and avoid hellfire. He connects the perfection of the heavens with God's comprehensive knowledge, emphasizing that earthly provisions are specifically designed for human benefit and spiritual reflection.
